title: Dispatch one typed Project display-name replacement

requirements.invariant: Renaming a Project is one distinct RenameProject outcome over stable AccountID and ProjectID. It is not Project details update, Client rename, Project archive or future Client reassignment, and it changes no other Project responsibility.

RenameProject changes only the current Project display name. It cannot change Client relationship, description, category/allocation/budget, media, lifecycle, child, accounting or history state, and display text never substitutes for stable Client identity or Transfer authority.

ProjectRenameIntent is a transient, non-Codable, exact Account/Project/revision/ProjectDisplayName presentation value. It owns no raw field, alternate validator, persisted form draft, initial/current read, readiness, lifecycle, dirty/no-op, dismissal, error-UX, route, provider identity or authorization claim.

ProjectRenameUseCase constructs the verified ProjectRenameDraft and RenameProjectCommand before invoking ProjectRenaming.rename exactly once, then validates and returns the exact receipt and LocalOperationState.

The use case preserves CancellationError and every ProjectRenameFailure. Only an unknown port error maps to localAcceptanceFailed; construction remains outside the port catch and receipt validation remains outside it.

Only the two new target leaves advance. ProjectRenameOperation/tests and ClientProjectDirectory stay verified; EditProjectModal, ProjectDetailView, ProjectDetailContainer, ProjectService/Protocol, Project model, ProjectFormValidation/tests and update_project retain their prior status and content because each owns broader responsibility.

Exactly two target-only executable leaves may change after READY. Physical persistence, optimistic projection, trusted authorization/audit/apply, Postgres/Data API/RLS/PowerSync/provider behavior, app/MCP wiring, source migration, hosted resources, production, release and cutover do not advance.

Verified dependency evidence EVID-PROJECT-RENAME-001 remains sole owner of accepted ProjectDisplayName bytes, ExpectedProjectRevision, the exact same-Project revision precondition, ProjectRenameDraft, RenameProjectCommand, subject, fingerprint, receipt validation and ProjectRenameFailure semantics. This use case consumes the already-validated name and composes those contracts without raw String normalization or semantic reimplementation.

items: ProjectRenameIntent is transient, non-Codable and exposes an exact public four-argument initializer for AccountID, ProjectID, ExpectedProjectRevision and ProjectDisplayName.
The use case reuses ProjectRenameDraft and RenameProjectCommand and accepts no raw String or alternate normalization rule.
Construction finishes before one ProjectRenaming.rename call; receipt validation follows the port boundary; all 12 typed failures and cancellation remain exact while unknown errors are bounded.
No initial/current read, readiness, lifecycle, dirty/no-op, UI or broader Project mutation policy is added.

items: Implementation may change only the two provider-free target leaves; every source app, service, model, validation, MCP and provider surface remains unchanged.
The deterministic in-memory test port cannot physically persist, authorize, synchronize, deploy, display, migrate, release or cut over a Project rename.

verification.expected: A non-@testable consumer constructs the exact public four-field ProjectRenameIntent. It is compile-time Equatable/Sendable, runtime non-Codable, stores no raw String, and preserves zero and UInt64.max revisions exactly.

An already-validated ProjectDisplayName, including accepted outer/interior whitespace and more than 8 KiB Unicode, reaches draft and payload byte-exactly after one call; the use case accepts no raw String and performs no second normalization.

Every LocalOperationState returns in the exact validated receipt after exactly one call carrying one Project rename and one same-Project expected-revision precondition; revisions zero and UInt64.max dispatch exactly.

A reciprocal flattened encoded-leaf matrix independently varies Account, Project, revision, typed display name, Operation, actor, contract and time against literal flattened baseline expectations and exact literal changed-leaf sets for all eight axes. Recording/canned fakes and expectation helpers must not reconstruct expected commands with ProjectRenameDraft, RenameProjectCommand or production validation logic.
Positive infinity and NaN capture times fail during construction with zero calls, while a mismatched receipt fails after exactly one call; neither is reclassified as a port failure.

All 12 ProjectRenameFailure values deliberately thrown by the port remain exact after one call, CancellationError remains structured cancellation, and only an unknown port error maps to localAcceptanceFailed.
All 12 diagnostic codes remain an exact stable enumeration and reveal no synthetic identity, Project name, raw error, credential, service payload or production identifier.

Exact nested command topology exposes only draft/envelope/subject/fingerprint ownership, typed replacement display name and one expected-revision precondition—never raw-name, Client, description, category, allocation, budget, media, lifecycle, child, accounting, history, UI or service detail.
